SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Nitrogen gas only

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

3. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

5. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

9. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

10. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Removing all vegetation

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.

12. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

2. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

3. A — Producers

4. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

5. D — Ice melting to water

6. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

7. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

9. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

10. B — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

12. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
